PullRequest.Title: Make copilot work in any terminal with a native Copilot CLI shim
PullRequest.Body:

Makes `copilot` work in any terminal when VS Code is installed, without bundling GitHub Copilot CLI. VS Code ships a small native `copilot` shim that runs the user's Copilot CLI, or offers to install it when there's none.

Feature: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#7531. Design: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9765.

## Changes

**Native `copilot` shim** (`copilot_shim/`, a new Rust crate)
- Ships in client and server builds at `bin/copilot-shim/copilot` (`copilot.exe` on Windows), next to the `code` command but in its own folder.
- Runs the first real Copilot CLI on `PATH` with the original arguments, terminal I/O and exit code. It skips itself, other copies of the shim, and the old script shims, so it can't recurse.
- When there's no Copilot CLI, it asks before installing it. On Windows it downloads GitHub's per-user MSI, checks its SHA-256 and its `GitHub, Inc.` Authenticode signature, and installs it without elevation. On macOS it uses Homebrew or the official script; on Linux, the official script.
- VS Code never updates or uninstalls Copilot CLI or its data.

**Windows setup** (`build/win32/copilot.iss`, included from `code.iss`)
- A **GitHub Copilot CLI** page: install it now, install it the first time you run `copilot`, or don't add `copilot` to `PATH`. It's skipped when a Copilot CLI is found, when the policy turns it off, and when the User Installer runs elevated.
- Without a choice on the page, `copilot` follows the *Add to PATH* task. Silent installs can use `/copilotcli=install|onfirstuse|none`. The choice is remembered, and background updates never download anything.
- Setup publishes the shim itself, renaming a running copy aside the way inno_updater does, so an open Copilot session never blocks an update. Uninstall removes only the shim and its `PATH` entry.
- Fixes the uninstall `PATH` cleanup guard (`if not CurUninstallStep = usUninstall`).

**Copilot extension**: integrated terminals use the native shim, appended to `PATH`, instead of the JavaScript, PowerShell and batch shims, which are removed. Builds without the shim can use a local build for development.

**Policy**: `CopilotCliCommand` (setting `chat.copilotCliCommand.enabled`, from 1.143) turns all of this off: no Copilot page, no `copilot` on `PATH`, and no installs. A Copilot CLI installed separately isn't affected. The Agent Host enforces it.

**Build**: the shim is built and signed in the CLI jobs for every target, packaged with the client and server, and tested in PR CI (`Linux Copilot Shim`).

Requirements and behavior: `copilot_shim/REQUIREMENTS.md` and `copilot_shim/SHIM_POST_INSTALL.md`.

## How to test

The Windows (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9843 to #9855) and macOS and Linux (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9880 to #9885) test plans have all been run. Setup and troubleshooting: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9979.

Run on this branch, rebased on `main`:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --locked` in `copilot_shim` | Passed, 71 tests |
| `node --test lib/test/*Policy*.test.ts lib/test/policyConversion.test.ts lib/test/policyDataMerge.test.ts` in `build` | Passed, 73 tests |
| `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `extensions/copilot` | Passed, 0 errors |
| `vitest run` on `copilotCLITerminalIntegration.spec.ts`, `copilotCLINativeShim.spec.ts`, `copilotCLIChatSessions.spec.ts` in `extensions/copilot` | Passed, 53 tests |
| `tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` | No new errors: same output as `main` with the same local dependencies |

Not run locally: `npm run export-policy-data -- --check` (needs a built Code OSS) and a full installer build; CI covers both.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The exhaustive loop, per-entry filesystem boundaries, and per-launch call path are explicit. Exact latency varies with PATH contents, but trailing network or disconnected entries are a realistic trigger and were not reached by the prior first-match command lookup.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem metadata operations and reads of candidate executables/scripts
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every invocation performs one candidate lookup per PATH directory on Unix and four per directory on Windows, plus canonicalization/metadata/identity calls for hits and up to 16 MiB of reads for each later small candidate; cost grows with PATH length and with shim copies after the selected CLI.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased command startup latency and lower interactive throughput, with especially large stalls when trailing PATH entries are disconnected drives, UNC paths, or slow mounts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted script shims delegated command resolution to the shell/Get-Command, which stopped at the first matching real `copilot`; PATH entries after that command were not touched on the launch critical path.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: `select_candidate` calls `discover`, and this added loop always inspects every unique PATH directory and every platform candidate name before returning the result, even though normal launch later selects only the first usable candidate.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `for directory in directories` loop at line 134 has no early-exit path and fills `DiscoveryResult`; `app.rs:297` invokes this on every launch, while `app.rs:252-267` consumes candidates in order and returns the first usable one.
Findings.Title: Stop PATH discovery after the first launchable CLI
Findings.Impact: Running `copilot` with an already-installed CLI early in PATH still probes every trailing entry. On enterprise Windows configurations with long PATHs and stale network/drive entries, each invocation can block on dozens of filesystem probes before the CLI starts.
Findings.Evidence: `candidate.rs:134-147` exhaustively walks all directories; on Windows `CANDIDATE_NAMES` has four names. `runtime.rs:158-192` shows each hit incurs symlink metadata, canonicalization, metadata, file identity, and executable checks. `candidate.rs:260-289` additionally opens each non-current candidate up to 16 MiB and scans it for shim markers. The normal launch caller only needs the first usable candidate, so all work after it is unnecessary; exhaustive diagnostics are only needed for installer PATH filtering.
Findings.Recommendation: Provide an ordered, short-circuiting discovery mode/iterator for `select_candidate`, stopping once a candidate is resolved as launchable while continuing past shims or unusable scripts. Keep the existing exhaustive collection only for `installer_path`, which genuinely needs every shim directory.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous wait and the two network boundaries are directly traced and bounded. The exact prevalence depends on network conditions and how long the user spends on earlier pages, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: two sequential HTTPS HEAD requests and synchronous wizard-thread waiting
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The delay is bounded at six seconds per interactive setup run, but approaches the full bound on offline, proxy-autodiscovery, filtered, or high-latency networks; requests are sequential rather than parallel.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased installer latency and a visibly blocked setup critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, leaving the Select Tasks page did not launch or wait for Copilot release-network probes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added NextButtonClick handler calls `CopilotWaitForProbe` before navigation can continue; that method loops on the UI thread until the result appears or `CopilotProbeWaitMs` (6000 ms) elapses.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1101 synchronously invokes `CopilotWaitForProbe`; added lines 532-539 wait in a Sleep loop for up to 6000 ms.
Findings.Title: Do not block installer navigation on the download probe
Findings.Impact: An interactive Windows install with no existing Copilot CLI can pause for roughly 5-6 seconds when the network or corporate proxy is unavailable, even if the user intends to choose “install on first use” or “don’t add.”
Findings.Evidence: `CopilotStartProbe` launches the shim with network enabled for the user installer. `setup/mod.rs:257-353` performs a HEAD to `/latest`, follows its release tag, then performs a second HEAD for the MSI asset, under a five-second probe deadline. `copilot.iss:523-541` converts that background work into a blocking marquee wait when the user leaves Select Tasks.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the probe off the navigation critical path: show the basic choices immediately and update download details asynchronously if the probe finishes, or defer release probing until the user explicitly selects “Install now.” Preserve a timeout for the eventual install operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch `copilot` when a real CLI is already installed, from an external or integrated terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Invocation parsing, exhaustive CLI discovery, candidate resolution, then exec/spawn of the real CLI must complete before the CLI can accept input. All discovery filesystem work is on the startup critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect the running shim and candidate names in every unique PATH directory; canonicalize/stat/identify hits and scan small candidates for shim markers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For D unique PATH directories: D lookups on Unix or 4D on Windows, plus several metadata calls and up to 16 MiB read per existing small non-current candidate. No grouping beyond exact duplicate-directory removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted shell/PowerShell shims resolved the first matching command and did not inspect trailing PATH entries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All probes finish before the first candidate is returned, including entries after the selected CLI, so slow mounts or disconnected drives directly delay startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the selected CLI, replacing the shim on Unix or waiting for it on Windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One final CLI process per invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy shim also launched one final CLI process, although it additionally ran a version probe.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required product work after discovery; not a regression by itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique PATH directory count, four candidate suffixes per directory on Windows, number and size of small candidate files, and latency of filesystem-backed PATH entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is fully serial; the final CLI starts only after it completes. There is no limiter need because there is one invocation, but there is also no short-circuiting.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No positive or negative discovery cache is used; every invocation repeats all metadata and marker reads. OS filesystem cache may make local warm launches cheaper but does not avoid remote/disconnected entry latency.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: exhaustive iteration, boundary cardinality, and launch reachability are explicit in the added code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local short PATHs may hide the cost; enterprise PATHs containing UNC shares, mapped drives, automounts, or multiple VS Code shim copies can make it substantial.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: normal launch performs avoidable trailing PATH I/O after the first launchable CLI.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run `copilot` when no CLI is installed and accept first-use installation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial exhaustive discovery and expected-install-directory fallback occur before prompting. After consent, tool discovery, downloader/install subprocesses, and post-install rediscovery are required before the CLI can launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial PATH discovery, fallback directory discovery, installer-tool discovery, installer PATH filtering, and post-install rediscovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Multiple serial passes over D PATH entries; tool discovery independently searches for bash/curl/wget and brew, and installer filtering performs another exhaustive Copilot search.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy shim used shell command resolution and then installer commands; it did not perform these native exhaustive metadata passes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial passes precede the prompt; later passes occur only after explicit consent and are required to install/locate the CLI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the official install script with curl/wget, or invoke Homebrew/MSI installation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One route at a time; failed routes can fall through serially to the next available route.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The legacy shim also used npm/Homebrew/curl/wget network installation after consent, with different route order.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After consent, installation cannot progress without the selected network operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run downloader, installer script/Homebrew/MSI, then launch the installed CLI.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically downloader plus installer plus final CLI; more if earlier installer routes fail.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Legacy installation likewise used serialized installer subprocesses and a final CLI process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required after user consent; routes are serialized to avoid concurrent installs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: PATH size, number of available installer tools/routes, route failures, download size, and network latency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery and installer routes are serial. The installer does not burst concurrent network/process work; fallback routes execute only after failure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent discovery or negative cache; expected install directories are checked on every missing-CLI invocation. Successful installation ends the missing state; failures are retried on a later invocation only after a fresh prompt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call flow and boundary counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Install duration is dominated by external network/package-manager behavior, while repeated PATH passes vary by environment.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the launch discovery fan-out; post-consent network and subprocess work is necessary and serialized.

Scenarios.Scenario: Interactive Windows VS Code setup when Copilot CLI is absent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A shim probe starts in the wizard, and leaving Select Tasks synchronously waits for its result before the Copilot page can be shown. Publishing/installing later occurs after the user's selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Launch the temporary shim probe and poll its result INI file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One probe process and repeated result-file existence checks every 50 ms for up to six seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Copilot probe process or result polling existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The wizard thread blocks at page navigation until the probe completes or the wait bound expires.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the latest GitHub release and query MSI asset size using two sequential HTTPS HEAD requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two requests when policy allows, no CLI is found, and the user installer enables network probing; no cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Setup did not contact Copilot release endpoints before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Although executed in the probe process, setup waits synchronously for the result, moving network latency onto navigation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe PATH/registry-derived directories, write/read result INI files, publish the shim, and manage retired copies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One PATH scan plus small result/progress files; publication cleanup scans the shim directory once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These Copilot-specific files and scans did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery precedes network probing; result-file polling gates navigation. Publication occurs during install completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Network/proxy latency and failure behavior rather than collection size; wait is bounded to six seconds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Network work runs on one probe worker thread, but the two HEAD requests are sequential. Setup polls serially and blocks navigation; there is no coalescing need because only one probe is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No release metadata cache. The probe is guarded to one run per setup process, so it is not repeated within the same wizard.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the synchronous wait and exact network sequence are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users who spend enough time on earlier pages may hide the wait; immediate navigation or slow/offline corporate networks exposes nearly the full bound.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable regression: preflight network work blocks installer navigation before the user selects an install action.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot extension activation and opening an integrated Copilot terminal
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Activation checks for the shipped shim and removes stored legacy shims. `openTerminal` awaits this initialization, then resolves shell configuration and creates the terminal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat the shipped shim; if present, recursively remove the legacy global-storage shim directory. Development builds may instead read/compare and publish a local shim.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shipped-shim stat and one directory removal per extension instance; local-development publication reads at most two files capped at 16 MiB and scans one storage directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Activation wrote several script shim files into global storage before contributing that directory to PATH.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Activation/openTerminal waits for this work, but packaged builds perform only a bounded check and cleanup; local binary publication is development-only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Contribute or remove the shim directory from integrated-terminal PATH and create a terminal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One contribution update on initialization and per relevant configuration change; one terminal creation per user action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The extension contributed the generated script-shim directory, prepended to PATH.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for terminal creation; no changed IPC/network fan-out was found.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Size/content of the legacy storage directory and, in development, shim binary size up to 16 MiB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Initialization is represented by one shared promise, so concurrent terminal opens coalesce on the same work. Local development publication uses a lock and serializes competing hosts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The initialization promise coalesces work within the extension instance. Packaged activation deletes stale stored state rather than retaining a growing cache; local retired copies are cleaned on later activation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the activation flow; low magnitude for packaged builds.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Legacy storage is normally tiny; abnormal unrelated contents could enlarge recursive cleanup, but that is not a normal product trigger.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: work is once-per-activation, coalesced, and replaces prior shim-generation I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Build, sign, and package client/server artifacts with the native shim
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Platform CLI jobs compile the Rust shim and publish an artifact; product jobs wait for/download it before signing or packaging client/server builds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cargo release build plus formatting, tests, and clippy on selected x64 jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One target build per platform/architecture job; quality commands run on x64 jobs as configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The native shim crate and its build steps did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Artifact production can gate product packaging, though compilation is placed in parallel CLI jobs where possible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish/download the shim pipeline artifact between jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small archive per platform/architecture, downloaded once by each consuming packaging job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Consumers wait for the artifact before final packaging/signing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extract/copy the shim into client and server trees before signing/archiving.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extraction and up to two copies per product job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No shim file was mixed into products.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required packaging work with constant cardinality.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of supported platform/architecture jobs, not user input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Shim compilation shares the existing CLI job and sccache; product compilation proceeds in parallel until the explicit artifact join. Packaging copies are serial constant work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cargo compilation uses shared sccache; artifacts are immutable per build. No runtime cache concern.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the pipeline dependencies, uncertain for measured duration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Added CI duration depends on cache hit rate and pipeline scheduling; no evidence establishes a disproportionate regression beyond expected feature build cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: added build/artifact work is bounded and intrinsic to shipping the new binary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 68 changed files. Reported exhaustive per-launch PATH filesystem fan-out and synchronous Windows installer navigation waiting on two network probes. Checked first-use installation, extension activation, process supervision, cleanup, packaging, cache behavior, and effective concurrency; no other high-confidence diff-caused performance regression met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
